evidence.observation: The panel configuration loader. Each knob is resolved independently at call time as `env(key, fallback)` / `envInt(key, fallback)` / `envBool(key, fallback)`, i.e. an explicitly configured value (from process.env, populated by loadDotenv at module load) wins over the hardcoded default. Defaults are visible inline: port 8123, metadataRemoteTimeoutMs 15_000, log level 'info', format 'json', knowledge.baseUrl http://127.0.0.1:8421, proxyBaseUrl http://127.0.0.1:8096, agentTemplateDir ./data/agent-templates. Because the object is rebuilt on every call there is no memoization, so an explicit value supplied after import still wins over any earlier value.

Numeric precedence guard: `undefined` and empty string are treated as 'not configured' and return the fallback; a non-finite parse result (e.g. 'not-a-number', 'NaN') also returns the fallback. This is the boundary that makes an empty or malformed config fall through to the default tier instead of producing NaN.

Boolean precedence guard: `undefined`/empty string return the fallback; only the literals 'true' and '1' are truthy, so 'false' and any other string resolve to false when supplied. Absent config therefore yields the default (e.g. knowledgeLlmBinding.sync === true).

String precedence primitive: `process.env[key] ?? fallback` — only undefined/null fall through, so an explicitly set empty string is accepted as the configured value for string knobs (contrast with envInt/envBool, which treat '' as absent).

The declared panel/instance configuration surface: server host/port, metadataInstancesConfig path, metadataRemoteTimeoutMs, ui dist dir, log level/format (LogLevel union), knowledge service baseUrl/authToken/timeoutMs, knowledgeLlmBinding sync/proxyBaseUrl, and agentTemplateDir. `knowledge.serviceId` is documented as injected per-request from the request instanceId, marking the point where explicit request input enters configuration.

Instance selection: the request-supplied instance id (the explicit request input, carried by the x-tdai-service-id header in validate-panel-headers) is looked up in the configured registry. A match returns that instance's config; no match throws InstanceRegistryError(400, 'INVALID_INSTANCE') rather than silently falling back to a default instance, so explicit request input strictly outranks defaults.

Instance config vs default: `proxy_endpoint` is spread into the emitted record only when configured, so a configured proxy_endpoint (config tier) wins over the client-side `?? gateway_endpoint` fallback (default tier); when absent the key is omitted entirely so the consumer's default applies. gateway_endpoint is always the forwarding default.

Canonical request header name for the explicit request input that selects an instance: 'x-tdai-service-id'. The same header set is used inbound (panel validation) and outbound (kernel forwarding), so the request value propagates rather than being replaced by a configured default.

claims.claim: Panel configuration resolves every knob by precedence: an explicitly configured value (process.env, loaded over .env by loadDotenv) wins over the hardcoded default literal declared in loadPanelConfig (port 8123, metadataRemoteTimeoutMs 15_000, log level 'info', log format 'json', knowledge.baseUrl http://127.0.0.1:8421, proxyBaseUrl http://127.0.0.1:8096, agentTemplateDir ./data/agent-templates).

Empty, malformed, or out-of-domain configuration falls through to the default tier: envInt returns the fallback for '' and non-finite input, envBool returns the fallback for '' and treats only 'true'/'1' as true, and loadPanelConfig guards LOG_LEVEL/LOG_FORMAT against values outside their allowed sets (falling back to 'info'/'json').

loadPanelConfig rebuilds the config object from process.env on every call (no memoization), so an explicit input supplied after module import still takes precedence over any previously observed value, while string knobs accept an explicitly empty string as configured (env uses `??`, not an emptiness check).

Explicit request input selects the instance configuration: the x-tdai-service-id header value is resolved through InstanceRegistry.resolve, and an unmatched value throws InstanceRegistryError(400, 'INVALID_INSTANCE') instead of defaulting to any configured instance, so request input cannot be silently overridden by a default.

Instance-level config outranks the default fallback: a configured proxy_endpoint is emitted by listPublic and beats the client-side `?? gateway_endpoint` default, while an absent proxy_endpoint is omitted from the record so the gateway_endpoint default is what applies.

The three tiers compose in the order explicit request input > config > default: the request supplies the instance id (request input), the panel env config and the selected instance's metadata-instances.json entry supply configured values (config), and hardcoded literals plus the gateway_endpoint fallback apply only when neither of the higher tiers supplies a value.

conclusion: MemoryPanel's instance/panel configuration follows a strict three-tier precedence contract — explicit request input > config > default — and the contract is pinned by an executable precedence test. The request tier is the x-tdai-service-id header resolved through InstanceRegistry.resolve (unmatched input is rejected with 400 INVALID_INSTANCE, never silently defaulted). The config tier is the env-derived panel config produced by loadPanelConfig plus each instance entry from metadata-instances.json (e.g. proxy_endpoint). The default tier is the hardcoded literals in panel-config.ts and the gateway_endpoint fallback, and it is reached only when the higher tiers are absent (undefined/empty/malformed or omitted). MemoryPanel/tests/panel/config-precedence.test.ts encodes the contract as 12 assertions; because node_modules is absent, the identical assertions were executed offline against the real modules via .prale-eval/config-precedence-demo.mjs with import-safe dotenv/zod/vitest shims, and all 12 passed.
